A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and 11 fully readable pages. Text and rendered-page comparison establish identical research content. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original silence-bias analyses, detector evaluations, and AVH-Align ablations in Sections 3–4, Figures 2–5, and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical analyses and experimental results in Sections 3–4, including AVH-Align evaluations and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same AV-HuBERT features, normalization, alignment MLP, contrastive objective, inference pooling, and supervised variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same FakeAVCeleb and AV-Deepfake1M coverage, additional LAV-DF, AVLips and DFDC analyses, and original-versus-trimmed test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: RawNet2, MDS and AVAD in Table 1; AVAD and SpeechForensics in Table 2; and the same official-test baselines in Table 3.

E3.justification: Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 4.2 retain identical splits, sample counts, silence-trimming procedures, training settings, and AUC/AP metrics. The official-test evaluation protocol also matches.

E4.justification: The silence-threshold and duration analyses, trimming robustness tests, frame-score case studies, and component and architecture ablations are identical, including Figure 3, Figure 5, and Tables 4–5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 3 retains official-test AUCs of 85.24% for AVH-Align, 99.90% for AVH-Align/sup, and 98.44% for the silence classifier.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(4) are identical. Neither version adds or removes formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about leading-silence shortcuts, their impact on detection, and improved robustness through alignment learned from real data.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the speculative origin of leading silence, explanations of trimming effects, the pretraining-leakage discussion, and the applicability arguments in Section 5.

D1.justification: The architecture details, learning rates, scheduler, stopping criteria, pretrained checkpoints, preprocessing instructions, and code-repository link are identical.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 60 references and identical related-work and research-positioning discussions in Sections 2 and 5.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, dated 28 March 2025, to v3, dated 29 May 2025. The title, authors, prose, headings and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp shifts slightly. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–5, captions and body layout are unchanged; rendered pages 2–11 are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: The research text, methods, evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information are identical. The version/date stamp and its slight placement change do not meaningfully affect paper quality.
